{{nihongo|'''Tsutsumi Shrine'''|皷神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kita-ku, Okayama|Q855478|qid=Q855478|lt=Kita-ku}}, {{ill|Okayama|Q200078|qid=Q200078}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|Q132936|qid=Q132936}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and is traditionally regarded as the ninomiya of {{ill|Bitchū Province|Q1047514|qid=Q1047514}}. Its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. Its {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine crest}} is "Dancing Crane." {{nihongo|'''Tsutsumi Shrine'''|皷神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bitchū Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
'''Main deity'''
* Takatahime-no-Mikoto - wife of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto

'''Merged deities'''
* {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|Q65318|qid=Q65318}} - said to have pacified Kibi as one of the {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|Q9076804|qid=Q9076804}}
* Kibitakehiko-no-Mikoto - son of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto
* Sazumorihiko-no-Mikoto - local powerful clan chief who ruled this area as {{ill|Agatanushi|Q10746487|qid=Q10746487}}, father of Takatahime-no-Mikoto
* Tsukawakehiko-no-Mikoto - retainer of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto

== History ==
The '{{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031}}' and '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' include legends of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto pacifying Kibi, and this shrine enshrines figures related to that story.

In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=register of deities}} in the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' lists "Tsutsumi Shrine" in Kaya District of Bitchū Province, ranking it as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. It is said there were once five shrine buildings and it was called "Tsutsumi Gosha Daimyōjin"<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.okayama-jinjacho.or.jp/cgi-bin/jsearch.cgi?mode=detail&jcode=19062 Tsutsumi Shrine] (Okayama Prefectural Shrine Association).</ref>.
